_comment: THE onboarding's own proof, the full part1->sleep->gift->part2 arc through the real input/AI/UI path. Boot CLASSLESS (hotbar 3 slots at the spar), meet Relc, accept the spar, drive part-1 beats by real keys against the SHIPPED training_yard tutor_lines (opening/first_step/pool_empty/dash/aim/first_blood/watch/wrap -- wrap's line references sleep + 'I owe you something'), win vs the inert 0-damage dummies (seed-robust), then: item_gained is ABSENT until the gift node (accepting the spar no longer grants the spear), sleep -> class_gained{warrior} with the grants-listing toast, RE-TALK Relc for the gift node (item_gained relcs_spare_spear + the 'press I' teaching + given_spear_by_relc), press I and EQUIP the spear via the real UI, then walk the gate road with NO interact -- the proximity trigger fires the part-2 ambush (real_ones), the warrior+spear kit (hotbar 4 slots) + Relc ally win it (road_clear), and the gate opens onto the street. Seed 9. NOTE part-2 skill beats (skill_aim/skill_hit) are UI-manual-only -- WICombatAI never calls a spear-tagged skill by name under autoplay, and the part-1 'aim' beat already exercises the identical targeting UI, so part-2 asserts real_ones + road_clear (both deterministic) and leaves the skill beats to a player's hands / relc_tutorial's manual coverage.

steps._comment: The GDI sleep veil voices the level-1 kit as [Skill – X Obtained!] lines under the [Warrior Class Obtained!] proclamation, matching the toast's 4 grants. lines == 5 (1 class line + 4 skill lines) is the automated proof the FIRST class gain lists its grants; later level-ups already list theirs via skill_unlocked. Under QA the veil collapses but still emits this count.

RACE-SAFE: ui_sleep_veil_rendered (veil, call_deferred) and ui_toast_rendered (message_layer's async toast drain) are TWO independent async streams whose relative emission order is NOT guaranteed -- it depends on whether the toast queue was empty when the class toast was enqueued (a wall-clock condition). When the prior 'Autosaved' toast is still mid-hold the veil emit lands first (the old local behavior); when the queue has drained the class toast renders immediately, before the veil (the slow-CI-runner behavior that stalled this to a 10s timeout). from_start:true scans from index 0 so this wait matches the (unique) class-toast render regardless of where the veil wait above left the cursor -- immune to either order. Paired with message_layer's headless frame-bounded drain (QA_TOAST_HOLD_HEADLESS_SECONDS).
